views.name: flights_dim
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  flight_id,
  flight_no,
  scheduled_departure,
  scheduled_arrival,
  departure_airport,
  arrival_airport,
  status,
  aircraft_code,
  actual_departure,
  actual_arrival,
  CAST((strftime('%s', scheduled_arrival) - strftime('%s', scheduled_departure)) AS INTEGER) AS scheduled_duration_seconds,
  CASE
    WHEN actual_departure IS NOT NULL AND actual_arrival IS NOT NULL
    THEN CAST((strftime('%s', actual_arrival) - strftime('%s', actual_departure)) AS INTEGER)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS actual_duration_seconds
FROM flights
views.description: Normalized/clean projection of the flights table: preserves identifiers and timestamps, exposes derived scheduled_duration and actual_duration (in seconds) where possible. Useful as a canonical flights relation for joins, filtering by schedule vs actual, and for duration-based aggregations. | Use for: Compare scheduled vs actual durations for flights; Filter flights by departure/arrival airports or status; Aggregate delays or durations by aircraft or route

views.name: flight_schedule_ranked
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  flight_id,
  flight_no,
  scheduled_departure,
  scheduled_arrival,
  departure_airport,
  arrival_airport,
  status,
  aircraft_code,
  actual_departure,
  actual_arrival,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY departure_airport, arrival_airport ORDER BY scheduled_departure ASC) AS route_rank
FROM flights
views.description: Per-route (departure_airport -> arrival_airport) ranked list of flights ordered by scheduled_departure. Exposes route_rank so downstream queries can select Top-K upcoming or recent flights per route by filtering on route_rank. Useful for latest-per-route, next-N flights, or time-window snapshots. | Use for: Find next N scheduled flights per route; Select most recent flights per route when ordering by scheduled_departure; Correlate ticket sales or load with top-ranked scheduled departures

views.name: tickets_with_booking
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.ticket_no,
  t.book_ref,
  t.passenger_id,
  b.book_date,
  b.total_amount
FROM tickets t
LEFT JOIN bookings b
  ON t.book_ref = b.book_ref
views.description: Denormalized tickets joined to their booking header. One row per ticket with booking metadata (book_date, total_amount). Useful for analyses that need ticket-level details together with booking timestamp and booking amount. | Use for: Measure booking lead time by comparing book_date to flight schedule when joined to flights; Aggregate revenue by booking vs ticket; Filter tickets by booking date ranges or booking amount

views.name: ticket_flights_enriched
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  tf.ticket_no,
  tf.flight_id,
  tf.fare_conditions,
  tf.amount,
  f.flight_no,
  f.scheduled_departure,
  f.scheduled_arrival,
  f.departure_airport,
  f.arrival_airport,
  f.status,
  f.aircraft_code,
  bp.boarding_no,
  bp.seat_no,
  t.book_ref,
  t.passenger_id
FROM ticket_flights tf
LEFT JOIN flights f
  ON tf.flight_id = f.flight_id
LEFT JOIN boarding_passes bp
  ON tf.ticket_no = bp.ticket_no
  AND tf.flight_id = bp.flight_id
LEFT JOIN tickets t
  ON tf.ticket_no = t.ticket_no
views.description: Ticket legs (ticket_flights) joined to flights and seats/boarding when available. One row per ticket-leg enriched with flight schedule, status, seat assignment (if a boarding_pass exists), and ticket-level passenger/book info via tickets->bookings. Useful for per-leg revenue, seat/boarding assignment, and linking tickets to flight events. | Use for: Compute revenue per flight leg or per passenger; Identify assigned seats and boarding sequence per ticket leg; Analyze no-shows by comparing ticketed legs to boarding_passes presence

views.name: aircrafts_seats_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  aircraft_code,
  fare_conditions,
  COUNT(*) AS seat_count
FROM seats
GROUP BY aircraft_code, fare_conditions
views.description: Aggregate counts of seats by aircraft_code and fare_conditions. One row per aircraft_code x fare_conditions with seat_count. Useful for capacity planning, mapping seat-class capacity to aircraft models, and joining with flights to compute theoretical capacity. | Use for: Estimate available seats by class for a given aircraft; Combine with flights to compute potential capacity per flight; Compare seat distribution across aircraft models

views.name: bookings_agg_by_date
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  DATE(book_date) AS book_date,
  COUNT(*) AS bookings_count,
  SUM(total_amount) AS bookings_total_amount
FROM bookings
GROUP BY DATE(book_date)
views.description: Daily aggregates of bookings: booking_date (date), bookings_count and bookings_total_amount. One row per booking date. Useful for trend analysis, time series of booking volume and revenue, and joining to flight schedules by date. | Use for: Daily booking trends and revenue analysis; Correlate booking volume with flight schedules or promotions

views.name: flight_delay_metrics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  flight_id,
  flight_no,
  scheduled_departure,
  scheduled_arrival,
  actual_departure,
  actual_arrival,
  aircraft_code,
  CASE
    WHEN actual_departure IS NOT NULL THEN CAST((strftime('%s', actual_departure) - strftime('%s', scheduled_departure)) AS INTEGER)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS departure_delay_seconds,
  CASE
    WHEN actual_arrival IS NOT NULL THEN CAST((strftime('%s', actual_arrival) - strftime('%s', scheduled_arrival)) AS INTEGER)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS arrival_delay_seconds,
  LAG(actual_arrival) OVER (PARTITION BY aircraft_code ORDER BY scheduled_departure) AS prev_actual_arrival
FROM flights
views.description: Windowed delay metrics per flight: computes departure_delay_seconds and arrival_delay_seconds and the lag of actual times to calculate previous-flight gap per aircraft. One row per flight_id with previous flight's actual_arrival for same aircraft (if any). Useful for delay propagation, aircraft utilization and running analyses across flight sequences per aircraft. | Use for: Analyze delay propagation across flights for the same aircraft; Compute average delay statistics and previous-leg gaps; Identify flights with long turnaround times or insufficient connection buffers

views.name: airports_geo
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  airport_code,
  airport_name,
  city,
  coordinates,
  timezone
FROM airports_data
views.description: Normalized airports projection exposing airport identifiers and key descriptive fields (airport_name, city, coordinates, timezone). Useful for joins to flights and spatial/timezone-aware analyses. | Use for: Map flights to airport metadata; Timezone conversions and city-based aggregations; Spatial proximity queries when coordinates are unpacked
